convertibility_reason: Heavy pending order management with BuyStop/SellStop, order expiration logic, and pending order existence checks by comment matching. The strategy places stop orders at current price levels every tick, requiring tick-level pending order management and broker-specific order comment tracking that doesn't translate cleanly to Python backtesting frameworks.

other_exits: Pending orders expire after 1 day (ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED with expdate = current time + D1 seconds)

custom_logic_notes: Strategy places a BuyStop at CurrentAsk and a SellStop at CurrentBid every tick if no matching pending order already exists (checked by order comment 'B'+Symbol or 'S'+Symbol). Pending orders expire after 1 day. No market orders are used - only stop orders that trigger when price moves to the current Ask/Bid level, which means orders activate immediately or nearly immediately upon placement since stop price equals current price. The CheckPendingOrder function iterates from OrdersTotal() down to 0 inclusive (off-by-one: should be OrdersTotal()-1 to 0), checking order comments to identify existing pending orders for the same symbol and direction. Margin check is duplicated (lines 59-62 and 65-68 are identical). Volume validation checks min/max/step compliance.
python_conversion_notes: Pending order management with comment-based tracking is not natively supported in most Python backtest frameworks. The BuyStop/SellStop placement at current Ask/Bid essentially acts as market orders in backtesting. Order expiration logic (1-day) needs custom implementation. The off-by-one bug in CheckPendingOrder (iterating to index OrdersTotal() instead of OrdersTotal()-1) should be noted but preserved or fixed depending on conversion intent. Margin check duplication (lines 59-68) should be deduplicated. SL/TP are specified in point units (PriceSL=300 means 300 points = 30 pips on 5-digit), so Python conversion must apply _Point multiplication correctly for the symbol.
